prompt: Review this anchor as its assigned subagent. Enumerate ALL requirements, qualifications, edge cases and scenarios. Inspect all supplied implementation and test fragments and trace each aspect to implementation behavior and actual test assertions or justified TODO/N/A evidence. Passing tests and associations alone are insufficient. Follow helpers and capture every additional source dependency with cargo meta review read ANCHOR PATH [selector] before completing the report. Explain prerequisites for justified TODO tests; do not claim deferred behavior is implemented. Distinguish source inspection from commands actually executed. Write a JSON report containing reviewer, report, and requested_edits. Leave requested_edits empty only when every aspect is accounted for and no edits are needed. Otherwise list concrete changes, including missing tests or justified TODO tests with prerequisite comments. Run cargo meta review record ANCHOR REPORT_FILE to finish. After edits or stale-input rejection, run cargo meta review start ANCHOR and review the fresh inputs. The gate fails until a current report with no requested edits is recorded. Dependency capture is agent-declared.
coordinator_instructions: Review only your assigned anchor using the sage-review-checklist skill and its start/read/record workflow. Capture these instructions with start --instructions /tmp/anchor-review-instructions.txt. Use captured source context; do not import old approvals or uncaptured coordinator conclusions. Write only your anchor's validations directory and a unique report file under /tmp. Coordinate production, test, and association edits with the coordinator before making them because concurrent reviewers may capture the same files. Capture essential dependencies using review read; report any necessary association additions for coordinated handling. Existing TODO/N/A evidence must be individually justified and remain deferred; do not claim passing placeholders verify functionality. Distinguish source review from tests actually run. On a suspected behavioral violation, coordinate a regression test and follow the skill rather than rubber-stamping. Return a concise summary of the recorded outcome or precise unresolved finding. Do not commit or change unrelated files.

its implementation and tests. The saved context lets `cargo meta` check whether
that assessment still applies. Running tests remains a separate obligation.
The main agent discovers review work through a failing `cargo meta check` or
the shared Cargo validation test. Diagnostics identify the affected anchors,
explain why they need review, and direct the agent to the review skill. The
skill delegates one subagent per anchor, supplying its ID and an initial prompt.
The subagent obtains its source context through the review commands, so that
the saved inputs are the same inputs it consumes.

An interrupted or abandoned review therefore cannot fall back to an
older approval. Unknown or invalid anchor IDs are rejected before clearing any
record. Other anchors' directories are unchanged. A failed start cannot leave
an older output appearing to validate newly captured inputs.
The recorded-read command takes an anchor with an active review directory, a
workspace-relative source path, and a selector from
{spec}`meta.reviews.fragment_format`. A read without an explicit selector
selects the whole file. It appends the selected contents and selector directly
to that anchor's `input.json` before returning those same contents to the
reviewer. Repeated reads are retained in order. Reads outside the workspace,
invalid selections, and reads without an active unfinished review are rejected.
These fragments participate in the same freshness checks as the initial inputs.
Reviewers declare every additional source dependency through this command and
are responsible for the completeness of those declarations.
Recording takes a completed report in the format defined by
{spec}`meta.reviews.output_format` and an anchor with an active unfinished review.
It checks the inputs already stored in that anchor's directory against current
{spec}`meta.reviews.fragment_associations`, and verifies the anchor and version
metadata. Missing or stale inputs, an unknown anchor, an invalid report, or an
absent active review rejects recording. A changed input requires a new review
starting with `cargo meta review start`; recording never substitutes new source
text for the inputs the agent actually reviewed.
On success, recording writes `output.json` and updates the summary's recording
time, preserving `input.json` exactly. Other anchors' records are unchanged.
A completed report requesting edits is saved but cannot satisfy the gate under
{spec}`meta.reviews.decisions`. Incomplete publication cannot satisfy the gate;
readers must not accept a mixture of files from different review attempts.
The shared `cargo meta check` fails when any current specification anchor lacks
an up-to-date validation satisfying {spec}`meta.reviews.staleness`, with an
output satisfying {spec}`meta.reviews.output_format` and no requested edits
under {spec}`meta.reviews.decisions`. It loads all validation directories, checks
the layout and summary metadata, and compares the saved inputs with current
source. At least one test and implementation entry are required.
A validation for an anchor ID absent from the current specification also fails
the gate, even when every current anchor has a passing validation. Diagnostics
name that directory and direct the reviewer to remove obsolete records or
reconcile renamed anchors and start fresh validation. Checking and recording
do not silently delete stale anchor IDs. Invalid record formats, unsupported
schema/policy versions, and incomplete records fail the gate. CI and
workspace Cargo tests use this same gate; checking never creates approvals.
For every anchor requiring re-evaluation, `cargo meta check` and the shared
Cargo validation test must fail until the assigned review subagent successfully
runs `cargo meta review record` for that review. Starting a review, capturing inputs,
reading additional context, or drafting a report cannot satisfy the gate.
An interrupted, abandoned, or failed review remains failing; an older report
cannot stand in for the unfinished review.
Recording is necessary but not sufficient: the recorded report must be complete,
request no edits, and still match current inputs. Recording a report that
requests edits, or changing inputs after recording, leaves the gate failing.
Every required anchor must meet these conditions independently.
CLI and Cargo-test failures identify every anchor requiring re-evaluation and
explain why: missing or unfinished validation, changed inputs or associations,
unsupported versions, malformed records, or requested edits. Changed-input
diagnostics identify the affected fragment or association. Failures direct the
main agent to invoke `.agents/skills/sage-review-checklist/SKILL.md`; they do not
start reviews or alter saved records themselves.
The repository's `sage-review-checklist` skill instructs the main agent to start
one review subagent for each anchor requiring re-evaluation. Each subagent is
given the anchor ID and an initial prompt directing it to run
`cargo meta review start <anchor>` and evaluate the printed inputs. The main
agent supplies any extra instructions or source context as recorded review
The subagent uses `cargo meta review read` for additional source context and
`cargo meta review record` to save its completed report. Only one subagent owns an
anchor's active directory at a time; reviews for different anchors may run in
parallel. The main agent reconciles requested edits, coordinates changes, and
repeats the start/read/record cycle for affected anchors after edits, then runs
`cargo meta check` again. TODO/N/A evidence is reviewed under the same workflow.
Reviewers trace every requirement to implementation code, checking missing
cases and contradictory behavior. They consider the complete associated test
set and explain which assertions exercise which parts of the claim. They identify a plausible
violation and whether those assertions would detect it.
The scenario, expected outcome, and assertion should be clear from the body of
the test function itself. Parsing, fixture construction, and setup helpers are
reasonable. A call such as `verify_everything()` that hides the meaningful
assertions is insufficient evidence: request a clearer test body instead of
approving it from its name or annotation. Reviewers may read helpers to
understand the test, and capture additional helper fragments through the recorded-read command.
A helper edit outside the supplied files and captured reads does not invalidate a saved review. Running the tests can detect
behavioral changes, but the cached review covers only the snapshotted source.
Add implementation associations to include additional essential source files.
When reviewers suspect a bug, they add an anchor-associated regression test
that exercises the intended behavior and run it against the implementation.
A reproduced behavioral failure yields concrete requested edits, with the test,
command, and observed failure in the report. Do not treat a build or environment
failure as reproduction. If a test cannot reproduce the concern, or a reviewer
cannot work out how to write one, consult the user with the concern and attempts;
leave the affected review unresolved until the concern is resolved. New tests
or associations require starting a fresh review before recording a report.
The generated [anchor pages](../anchor/meta/reviews.html) report implementation entries,
annotated tests, explicit TODO/N/A gaps, and saved implementation/test reviews. These
associations do not themselves establish that a test ran.
